title: Needs vs Wants vs Demands Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 3
description:
Forty hungry students walk past Laddoo Lab's stall at the college gate, and only five buy a pack. Why? Because being hungry is not the same as wanting a laddoo, or being able to pay for one. In this animated lesson, Laddoo Lab, a tiny millet laddoo brand from a home kitchen in Bengaluru, helps us untangle three words every marketer uses.

You will see Kotler and Armstrong's definitions from Principles of Marketing: a need is a state of felt deprivation, a want is the form a need takes as it is shaped by culture and personality, and a demand is a want backed by buying power. We follow Mrs. Rao from her daughter's hunger to a sweet laddoo to a paid pack, then count live at the college gate as forty needs become twelve wants and five real buyers. We climb Abraham Maslow's five levels of needs from his 1943 paper, see needs, wants and demand at work today in a hospital, a phone maker and an airline, and look honestly at the human side: ads can make a want feel like a need, eating now and paying later is debt, not demand, and a 2019 study found that Maslow never drew the famous pyramid.

This is Episode 3 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
